metadata.title: Exploring the relationship between reading literacy and creativity competence: A multilevel modeling approach

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses the Hong Kong sample of OECD PISA 2022 and constructs student-level and school-level variables (reading literacy, creativity competence, and ESCS-based SES), with students nested in schools. The manuscript does not report applying PISA complex survey weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or replicate-weight procedures, and it instead focuses on multilevel path modeling in Mplus. Because the analysis is not framed as a survey-weighted estimation and no weight variable name is provided, the weighting strategy is unclear and may be omitted. The analytic dataset is further restricted by dropping cases with missing data on the two main variables (reading and creativity) and using Mplus full-information maximum likelihood (FIML) for remaining missingness on SES.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the Hong Kong sample of OECD PISA 2022. The analysis dataset included students with non-missing data on the two main variables (reading and creativity); cases missing on reading or creativity were dropped. The remaining missingness on SES was handled using full information maximum likelihood (FIML) in Mplus 8.11, with the manuscript reporting only 0.9% missing values on SES. School-level variables (school mean reading literacy, school SES, and school creativity) were computed by aggregating student-level measures within schools.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2022 Hong Kong (15-year-olds) Reading literacy → Creativity competence (overall score; 10 PVs)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Two-level path model (multilevel modeling in Mplus) — standardized paths: Reading → Creativity β = 0.44 (p < .01); SES → Creativity β = 0.04 (p < .01); Gender (0=female, 1=male) → Creativity β = −0.12 (p < .01). Model fit: χ2/df = 0.046/1, p = .833; RMSEA = 0.000; CFI = 1.000; TLI = 1.000; SRMR (within/between) = 0.001/0.000.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 Hong Kong the study leveraged Reading literacy (PISA PVs), Socioeconomic status (ESCS), and Gender to predict student creativity competence (PISA 2022 plausible values), finding that reading literacy had a strong positive association with creativity (β = 0.44, p < .01) while SES had a small positive association (β = 0.04, p < .01) and males scored lower than females (β = −0.12, p < .01). This indicates that strengthening reading literacy may be a high-leverage pathway for improving students’ creativity, though the cross-sectional design limits causal interpretation.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2022 Hong Kong (15-year-olds) School mean reading literacy → School creativity (overall score; 10 PVs aggregated)
main_findings.target_variable: School collective creativity competence (school-level aggregated score)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Two-level path model — standardized paths at the school level: School mean reading → School creativity β = 0.74 (p < .01); School SES → School creativity β = 0.31 (p < .01); School SES → School mean reading β = 0.60 (p < .01). Model fit: χ2/df = 0.046/1, p = .833; RMSEA = 0.000; CFI = 1.000; TLI = 1.000; SRMR (within/between) = 0.001/0.000.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 Hong Kong the study leveraged school mean reading literacy (PISA PVs) and school SES to predict school collective creativity competence, finding that school mean reading literacy showed a stronger positive association with school creativity (β = 0.74, p < .01) than school SES (β = 0.31, p < .01). This indicates that school-level reading literacy environments may be particularly important for nurturing collective creativity, suggesting that school resource and literacy initiatives could have broader peer-group effects.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes the Hong Kong sample of OECD PISA 2022 (15-year-olds; 5557 students nested in 163 schools) to examine how reading literacy relates to creativity competence at both student and school levels. Reading literacy and creativity competence are both represented using PISA plausible values, with the authors using all 10 plausible values and reporting average statistics; multilevel path modeling in Mplus is used to account for nesting. The model fit is reported as excellent (χ2/df = 0.046/1, RMSEA = 0.000, CFI = 1.000, TLI = 1.000, SRMR within/between = 0.001/0.000). At the student level, reading literacy strongly predicts creativity (β = 0.44, p < .01), while SES has a small positive effect (β = 0.04, p < .01) and gender shows males scoring lower (β = −0.12, p < .01). At the school level, school mean reading literacy is the strongest predictor of school creativity (β = 0.74, p < .01), with school SES also significant (β = 0.31, p < .01). Limitations include the cross-sectional nature (no causal claims) and unclear use of PISA sampling weights.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The manuscript uses multilevel modeling/path analysis in Mplus rather than machine-learning predictive algorithms; therefore, no ML techniques are evaluated and the ML fields are intentionally left empty. The extraction focuses on the empirical multilevel relationships between reading literacy, SES, gender, and creativity competence using PISA 2022 plausible values.
